name: Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani
role: President of Iran (1989–1997), parliamentary speaker and Expediency Council chairman
summary: Rafsanjani promoted privatization, foreign investment and postwar reconstruction within Iran’s Islamic Republic. He defended clerical government and opposition to Israel, while later advocating negotiations with the West, public consent and freer lawful debate. His earlier repression and implication in overseas political assassinations complicate that later reformist role.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: His reforms shifted allocation toward private enterprise and away from state controls.

public-ownership.rationale: He promoted privatizing state enterprises, without proposing privatization of every strategic sector.

regulate-corporations.rationale: His economic program reduced government controls to encourage business investment.

empower-police-military.rationale: His 2016 speech favors shifting military expenditure into productive activity, but he also explicitly defended strengthening Iran’s missile capability.

more-religion-public.rationale: He insists religious teaching and clerical guidance remain central to public government.

gradual-change.rationale: He explicitly advocates democratization through incremental steps.

free-trade.rationale: His administration established free-trade zones and pursued trade liberalization.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He insists on continuing Iran’s peaceful nuclear development and domestic fuel cycle.

revolution-justified.rationale: He praises the Islamic Revolution as a justified popular struggle and achievement to preserve.

central-planning.rationale: He sought a market-oriented economy in place of the previous state-centric allocation model.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He endorses the revolution’s removal of the Shah and its replacement by an Islamic republic.

democracy-best.rationale: He endorses democracy, but identifies it with Iran’s restricted Islamic electoral system.

political-violence-never.rationale: He defended Palestinian armed and suicide operations as resistance; the Mykonos court also implicated his leadership in political assassinations.

separate-church-state.rationale: His sermon insists the state must retain its Islamic as well as republican character.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He called for living by Islamic law while rejecting radical individuals’ harsh interpretations.

limit-population.rationale: His government introduced birth-spacing services, free contraception and explicit goals to reduce fertility and population growth.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He calls Israel illegitimate and anticipates its removal, while distinguishing Jewish people from Zionism.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: His government sought a major foreign contract to develop Iran’s offshore oil fields.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He rejected the Mykonos judgment implicating his government as political, though later urged sympathy for victims of the 2009 crackdown.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: He explicitly describes Israel’s establishment as a colonial project displacing Palestinians.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He says Islamic government cannot exist without the people and their votes.

party-controls-media.rationale: He calls for lawful media freedom and debate among all sides.

clerical-rule.rationale: He endorses the clerical Assembly of Experts selecting the supreme leader within the Islamic system.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: He later advocated peaceful nuclear development and disarmament, but acknowledged earlier consideration of a wartime deterrent.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He requires government, security forces and protesters alike to act within the law.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: He opened privatization and investment opportunities to foreign investors instead of a blanket exclusion.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His later demand to release protesters contrasts with earlier crackdowns and court findings implicating his leadership in dissident killings.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: He maintains hijab as an Islamic requirement while criticizing excessive strictness in its enforcement.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: He accepted World Bank-linked restructuring and subsidy reductions rather than rejecting lender-backed reforms.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: He honors those killed in the revolutionary and Palestinian struggles as martyrs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: He frames Palestinian resistance through divine justice, salvation and punishment for its enemies.

arms-reduction.rationale: He praises the economic benefits of Japan’s and Germany’s military restrictions, while retaining support for Iranian defensive missiles.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: He urges an international court to try those responsible for crimes against Palestinians.

notes: Researched all ten themes and checked the complete 490 statements against the evidence, including remaining nulls. Full 2009 sermon and 2001 Qods broadcast downloaded and searched. The IRIB interview was read in full through the web tool; direct HTTP download was forbidden. Mature 2009 statements prevail on lawful opposition and popular consent, with earlier repression and Mykonos findings retained explicitly as qualifications. The Mykonos case implicated the state leadership and committee including the president; Rafsanjani was not personally convicted in that trial. His nuclear scenario was controversial and later disputed by his office; it is not converted into an unqualified policy of launching a nuclear strike. His 2015 admission concerned historical contingency planning, not an announcement of a current bomb policy. Temporary-marriage advocacy does not establish sex outside marriage or legalization of sex work. His daughter’s women’s-rights positions are not attributed to him. Public-consent arguments do not establish secular liberal democracy or unrestricted candidate eligibility. No reliable specific positions found on most ecological, racial, immigration, labor and digital-rights statements. No inferred answers.
